quiz.title: Second Order Derivatives Quiz (Ex 5.7)
quiz.intro: Eight questions on second order derivatives, straight from the ideas in Exercise 5.7. Pick an answer for each, then press Check my score.
quiz.about: Class 12 Continuity and Differentiability — second order derivatives

questions.q: If y = x³, what is d²y/dx²?
questions.explanation: First derivative is 3x²; differentiating again gives 6x.

questions.q: If y = sin x, then d²y/dx² equals:
questions.explanation: y' = cos x and y'' = −sin x, so d²y/dx² = −sin x = −y.

questions.q: For y = e^(2x), the second derivative d²y/dx² is:
questions.explanation: y' = 2e^(2x), y'' = 4e^(2x). Each derivative brings down another factor of 2.

questions.q: If y = log x (x > 0), then d²y/dx² equals:
If y = cos x, which relation does y satisfy?
questions.explanation: y' = −sin x and y'' = −cos x = −y, so y'' + y = 0.

questions.q: If y = e^x, what is the value of y'' − y?
questions.explanation: Every derivative of e^x is e^x, so y'' = y and y'' − y = 0.

questions.q: If y = x² + 3x + 2, then d²y/dx² is:
questions.explanation: y' = 2x + 3, and differentiating again the constant 3 vanishes, leaving y'' = 2.

questions.q: If y = tan x, then d²y/dx² equals:
questions.explanation: y' = sec²x; using the chain rule, y'' = 2 sec x (sec x tan x) = 2 sec²x tan x.

faq.q: What is Exercise 5.7 of Class 12 Maths about?
faq.a: Exercise 5.7 of the Continuity and Differentiability chapter deals with second order derivatives. You differentiate a function once to get dy/dx, then differentiate that result again to get d²y/dx².

faq.q: How do you find a second order derivative?
faq.a: Find the first derivative dy/dx using the usual rules, simplify it, and then differentiate that expression a second time with respect to x. The result is written as d²y/dx² or y''.

faq.q: Why do many Ex 5.7 problems ask you to prove a relation?
faq.a: Several questions give a function and ask you to show it satisfies an equation such as y'' + y = 0 or y'' − y = 0. You compute y' and y'', substitute them in, and confirm both sides match — this checks that you can handle the derivatives correctly.

faq.q: What are the second derivatives of the standard functions?
faq.a: Useful ones to remember: for sin x it is −sin x, for cos x it is −cos x, for e^x it is e^x, for log x it is −1/x², and for x^n it is n(n−1)x^(n−2).
